summary: This program models simple houseplant care with four small methods, each showing a different return type: one that returns nothing, one that returns a true/false value, one that returns a whole number, and one that returns text. The main method calls each one in turn and prints the results.

lines.text: Declares the class that holds the whole program; because the file is run directly, the class name must match the file name GrowPlant.java.
The main method is where Java begins execution, so every instruction the program performs starts from here.
Calls a method that only performs an action and hands nothing back, so the call stands alone as a complete statement.
The call to hasSunlight() is replaced by the value it returns, and joining that value to a string with + converts the boolean into the text "true".
Here the returned number 3 is glued onto the label, which shows that any return type can be printed the same way.
The returned String is combined with the label to produce one line of output.
The keyword void means this method returns no value at all; it exists purely for the side effect of printing a message.
Declaring the return type as boolean promises that this method will hand back either true or false.
The return statement sends the value back to whoever called the method and immediately ends the method.
An int return type means the caller receives a whole number, which is useful for counts and measurements.
A fixed value is returned here to keep the focus on return types; a real program would measure the soil instead.
A String return type lets a method hand back a piece of text that the caller can print or examine.
